verses.text: Yahweh, you are my God. I will exalt you! I will praise your name, for you have done wonderful things, things planned long ago, in complete faithfulness and truth.
For you have made a city into a heap, a fortified city into a ruin, a palace of strangers to be no city. It will never be built.
Therefore a strong people will glorify you. A city of awesome nations will fear you.

For you have been a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat, when the blast of the dreaded ones is like a storm against the wall.
As the heat in a dry place will you bring down the noise of strangers; as the heat by the shade of a cloud, the song of the dreaded ones will be brought low.
In this mountain, Yahweh of Armies will make all peoples a feast of choice meat,  a feast of choice wines, of choice meat full of marrow, of well refined choice wines.
He will destroy in this mountain the surface of the covering that covers all peoples, and the veil that is spread over all nations.
He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.
It shall be said in that day, “Behold, this is our God! We have waited for him, and he will save us! This is Yahweh! We have waited for him. We will be glad and rejoice in his salvation!”
For in this mountain Yahweh’s hand will rest. Moab will be trodden down in his place, even like straw is trodden down in the water of the dunghill.
He will spread out his hands in the middle of it, like one who swims spreads out hands to swim, but his pride will be humbled together with the craft of his hands.
He has brought the high fortress of your walls down, laid low, and brought to the ground, even to the dust.

footnotes.content: See how the prophet begins with exaltation—not flattery, but wonder at God's character. He's dwelling on those 'wonderful things planned long ago,' the ancient faithfulness of a God who thinks centuries ahead. When our hearts grow small with today's troubles, looking back at His kept counsel steadies us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The proud city—once it seemed unshakeable. Now it's a heap. The prophet isn't gloating; he's teaching us that the strongholds we fear have never been anything but sand in God's hand. What fortress looms large in your sight today? He sees it as already dust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here's the strange reversal: the strong people glorify Him *because* He's humbled the proud. It's not that God shows weakness; it's that He shows mercy to the small while bringing low the arrogant. That's the fear of the Lord that wisdom begins with—recognition that power without mercy is only cruelty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Notice the imagery: stronghold, refuge, shade. These are the words of someone who *lives* in vulnerability—poor, needy, distressed. The prophet knew that God's protection isn't doctrine to the weak; it's their daily bread. When the blast comes, the shade holds. When it's all too much, He is enough.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The noise of strangers, the song of the dreaded ones—both are brought low. Not by our strength, but as surely as a cloud cools the scorching heat. The oppressor's voice that once seemed loud and endless will shrink to nothing. In God's time, He quiets what shouts against His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Suddenly—a feast. On *this mountain*, where judgment just fell, there's abundance for 'all peoples.' Marrow and wine, the richest things. It's as if the prophet sees past the wreckage to a table where enemies and strangers are invited to eat. That's the generosity of a King whose victory includes a feast.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: That 'covering,' that 'veil' laid over all nations—it blinds us to God's glory and to one another's humanity. When He tears it away, we see truly. The barriers that kept us divided, afraid, and small fall away. What veil keeps you from seeing the Lord's face and your neighbor's worth?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo here of the One who rose on the third day. Death—the last enemy, the one that silences all of us—has been *swallowed up*. That a grandparent can sit reading these words with the hope of resurrection burning in their chest is because Someone made this promise walk. Tears will not be our end.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Behold, this is our God'—not 'could be' or 'might be,' but recognition settled in the heart. They waited for Him. The waiting wasn't wasted; it was the very thing that opened them to see His face. When He comes, the faithful recognize Him. There's no mistaking His salvation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moab was Israel's longtime foe. Here, Moab gets trodden 'like straw in the water'—not grand or terrible, just trampled like a thing of no account. The prophet is saying to Israel's remnant: yes, those who harassed you will come to nothing. The Lord's hand at rest does what your sword could never do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He spreads His hands like a swimmer—that image carries both gentleness and power. He moves through the waters with mastery, but the gesture is open, not clenched. Meanwhile, Moab's pride drowns; the craft of his hands—all his schemes and strategies—are humbled with him. In God's presence, all noise quiets.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The high fortress comes down to dust. What a lesson in the brevity of human grandeur. The walls that took years to raise, that promised safety to thousands, that seemed eternal—all of it ends in dust. Only one kingdom endures. Only one throne stands. That's the comfort of knowing which side we're on.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
